author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새 수만 마리 · 여름철새 수백 마리 · 겨울철새 수백 마리
habitat: 해안 모래밭, 염전, 갯벌, 휴경지, 모래가 발달한 강 하구
summary: 흔한 나그네새로, 일부 무리는 해안 모래밭, 휴경지, 염전 주변, 모래가 많은 강 하구 등에서 지역적으로 번식하고 일부는 겨울도 난다. 해안 모래밭이나 염전, 갯벌 등에 살며, 빠르게 뛰다가 멈춰 갯지렁이나 작은 갑각류를 잡고 다시 달려가는 행동을 되풀이한다. 모래땅을 오목하게 판 둥지에 옅은 갈색 바탕에 검은 무늬가 있는 알 3개를 낳고, 암수가 번갈아 24~26일 동안 품는다. 북반구 온대에서 번식하고 겨울에는 남쪽으로 옮겨 간다.

art.subject: Kentish Plover (Charadrius alexandrinus), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean beaches and salt pans from April to July: forehead and short supercilium white; a black bar across the forecrown above the white forehead; crown and nape rufous-cinnamon, variable in brightness; narrow black eye-stripe from the bill through the eye to the ear-coverts; a white collar across the hindneck; upperparts plain sandy grey-brown; underparts white; a black patch on each side of the upper breast, not meeting in the centre. Short, slender black bill; dark eye; dark grey to blackish legs with a pinkish tinge.
art.pose: running across wet sand, pausing to pick at a small crustacean
art.scene: Korean coastal sand beach beside a tidal mudflat and salt pans in May, bright late-spring light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view standing: rufous crown, black forecrown bar above the white forehead, narrow black eye-stripe, white hind collar, sandy upperparts, black breast-side patch, pinkish-black legs
adult male breeding, front view standing: white underparts with the two black breast-side patches clearly separated in the middle, white forehead under the black forecrown bar
adult female, side view standing: sandy-brown crown, little or no dark forecrown bar, brown eye-stripe and brown breast-side patches, white collar and white underparts
art.build: Small, pale plover, 17.5cm, a little larger than a sparrow, with a large rounded head, short neck and plump body on fairly long legs; runs fast, stops abruptly and tilts forward to pick. Bill black, short and thin, clearly shorter than the head. Legs medium length, dark grey. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. Tail short, dark-centred with white sides. In flight a narrow white wing-bar and white tail sides.
avoid: Do not paint a complete breast band — that is Little Ringed or Common Ringed Plover.
Do not paint a yellow eye-ring (Little Ringed Plover) or an orange-based bill (Common Ringed Plover).
Do not paint yellow or orange legs.
Do not paint a dark brown back; the upperparts are pale sandy grey-brown.
